APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF FEBRUARY 4, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:04 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member– present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 12.4 there is a change it says $32,700 it should read $40,000.

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  4-0 (Councilmember Ancona absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.3.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:08 pm. Councilmember Ancona did not participate in Closed
  Session. Councilmember Ancona joined the City Council at 7:00 pm.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:00 pm.

  City Attorney Rick Olivarez reported out of Closed Session with respect to Items
  4.1 through 4.3.

  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

15.  CITY ATTORNEY’S AGENDA: No material submitted.

16.  CITY MANAGER’S AGENDA:

  16.1  Discussion Regarding Charter City, City Council Expansion and District
  Elections.

  Charles Hoffman – All I could say is that the charter for lack of a better word is
  Greek to me. I have been looking on the internet trying to figure out a little bit
  about it because I have no idea. My thing is, is this going to be better for us than
  what we have right now and also what is this going to cost me as a taxpayer?
  We are talking salary, we are talking about a permanent Mayor and I am one of
  these I really do believe this I am sorry to see we elect our Mayor for a two year
  term. I don’t know why whoever it is not a four year term. I am glad to get
  exposure I am sure in the future if we go this route you will have community
  meetings to discuss this.

17.  WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS: No material submitted.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Quintero

  City Manager Martinez – Just wanted to remind everyone and invite community
  members to attend Coffee with the City Manager on Saturday and the purpose of
  that is to incentivize and invite the community to apply for the different
  commissions available and to engage them civically in City business. I think it
  would be a wonderful time to get to know the different Department Directors, the
  different programs we are working on, the different projects we are working on
  and just to get an open door policy for the community to come in and really be
  engaged. We also have, we are going to be doing a groundbreaking for the
  charging stations and the Ramona Project it is going to be a very busy day for
  the Council. You are going to see the fruit of our labor and all the things you
  approved and your made decisions on you are going to see them coming to
  fruition after many years. I hope to see you all on Saturday for three back to
  back events.

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Morales

  I just wanted to say thank you to staff for pushing on the skate park and I am just
  elated that the community of boys and girls are going to have an opportunity to
  go out there and have a great time so looking forward to moving on that. Just
  wanted to get a sense of, I know we are putting together the newsletter and just
  wanted to put the word out that it is going to be mailed out sometime next week
  so that you can keep an eye out and take a look at some of the great projects
  that are coming to fruition and those that are down the pipeline. I thought we did
  a magnificent job and when I say we inclusive but frankly it was staff putting it
  together and really highlighting a lot of the work that is happening in the City.
  Often times when residents are a little bit concern with respect to the movement
  and why we are not moving along I think the newsletter is definitely something
  tangible that I wish I would bring with me every day to show really what we are
  doing and all of the work that is down the pipeline and why it is that staff is busy
  every single day so with that thank you staff for the work that you do. Thank you
  Chief and your Officers that are here making sure that you are responsive
  especially during this last week when we had trees coming down on cables

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 4, 2020

  raising havoc in our community and I know that our Department is quick to
  respond so thank you and have a good night.

18C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  Since we got into the topic of Art in Public Places just wanted to see if we can get
  an update on maybe some potential projects coming up.

  City Manager Martinez – We do have some potential projects. We are working
  on a big mural of El Monte past, present and future and the different components
  and the historical importance of it. I have a draft that was prepared muralist
  Ignacio Gomez and he is syndicated.

  Councilwoman Ancona – I know in regards to our Ad Hoc meetings it has been a
  minutes since we have met so I am not sure if we need to schedule those
  meetings just to get updates on what we have going on, what is coming up.

  City Manager Martinez – We have had the Development Ad Hoc and Fiscal Ad
  Hoc meetings.

  Councilmember Ancona – We do need Homeless and Parks.

  City Manager Martinez – And Public Works. I will be reaching out to you all to
  schedule those meetings.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  In regards to overnight parking I know that the City of La Verne has a very
  successful program where you purchase a permit online and you place it on your
  dash and it allows you overnight and there is also an opportunity long month
  parking. So that we are not recreating the wheel when it comes to overnight
  parking there are resources out there and cities that do have programs on
  overnight parking so I would love to see something like that come to the City
  Council very soon. There has been a lot of talk about parks today and one of the
  things that I requested about a year ago and was presented but I think it is time
  for an update and that is our park inventory meaning an opportunity for our Public
  Works team to walk around and tell us what needs to be fixed. It really upsets
  me whenever we have families that come from Zamora Park or Gibson Mariposa
  or form Lambert Park and they show us equipment that is broken and not that it
  is only broken but that it has been broken for a month or two and yet we haven’t
  taken the initiative to fix it that is frustrating. Let’s take another walk through and
  get us an updated inventory sheet in regards to what needs to get fixed. We
  need a thorough walkthrough is it a door at Arceo Park, is it a faucet at Mountain
  View Park even some of these little things as long as we have a list then we have
  a goal of items that we can start checking off and increasing the safety as well as
  the usability of our parks. No one wants to go to a park where they don’t feel
  safe or where they feel the amenities are working that is frustrating. I look
  forward to seeing an updated park inventory of things that need to be fixed.
  Don’t forget February 22nd we will be doing a ribbon cutting for Fletcher “Fetch”
  Park. We talk about ideas that have been in the board for a very long time and I
  think it is very exciting that Fletcher “Fetch” Park will be coming to fruition very
  soon as well. Recognizing our conversations years ago about what a dog park
  should be named and coming up with Fletcher “Fetch” our parks and rec team
  were very excited about this. Happy birthday Bobby Muela, 23 years old today I
  wish I could of celebrated with you I know you are not watching because you are
  at dinner but I just wanted to make sure that you knew I was thinking of you and
  with that City I appreciate the opportunity to be your Councilwoman have a good
  evening and there are any questions feel free to give us a call at City Hall. One
  last thing one student has been here since 6:00 pm Giselle Cruz I just wanted to
  say thank you for being here an Arroyo Alumni and now a current student at Cal
  State Fullerton it is people like you that we pull for and we hope that you not only
  get a good education but that you get that education and you come back to El
  Monte and you inspire other young people to do the same.

18E.  Councilman Velasco

  18E.1 Discussion Regarding the DEMBA Sponsored Lunar New Year
  Celebration on Main Street on Saturday, February 8, 2020.

  This is going to happen I spoke to the director of DEMBA and it will
  happen this Saturday from 12:30 pm to 4:00 pm at the Valley Mall. They
  are going to have the dragon, the celebration, sales and gifts so come on
  by we are going to be there from 12:30 pm to 4:00 pm. Volunteer
  recognition dinner for Meals on Wheels it is on Thursday, February 13,
  2020 at El Sombrero it is a fundraiser $20 per person and as you all know
  Meals on Wheels is a non-profit organization that everybody helps and
  tries to help but they need more donations. They are going ot have their
  installation dinner try and buy your tickets at the Museum with Cathi
  Eredia. We also invite you to the groundbreaking of the Ramona/Valley
  at 11:00 am on Saturday, February 8th. I keep bring up the census it is
  very important. March is coming up and you will be getting the
  notifications we need everyone to be counted it is a non-partisan activity
  and there are $675 Billion Dollars of federal funding nationwide. Every
  city will receive funding depending on the number of people that they
  register.

  18E.2 Discussion Regarding Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs).

  We spoke about the ADU already so we will wait for answer later.

  18E.3 Discussion Regarding Overnight Parking.

  We don’t have to have a discussion we have already talked about this
  over and over I think that it is time that we really take it serious and since
  we have that Ordinance that we just passed then we have to assure
  overnight parking. I think it is time that we look into how we are going to
  establish overnight parking. We had already recommended several years
  ago that maybe we can start in certain sections of the City and that is for
  the staff to decide what part of the City we could start instead of doing the
  whole citywide no overnight parking. Let’s start in a certain section and
  let’s try it out. We have to move on this.
